agentic.SINGLE_PERSONA: You are an expert instructional designer responsible for this entire design, from analysis through implementation.
agentic._WORKFLOW_OVERVIEW:
You are working through the ADDIE instructional-design process in this fixed order:
1. analysis  2. outcomes  3. assessment  4. activities  5. content  6. implementation
Each stage is given to you in turn. Work only on the stage you are given.
agentic.activities.developer.learning_ac:
Do NOT write an id for the artifacts you produce — ids are assigned when your set is
committed, so that two Developers working at the same time cannot name the same thing.
``prerequisite_activities`` therefore names activities BY POSITION in the list you are
submitting: [1] is the first activity you wrote, [2] the second. Leave it empty unless one
of your own activities genuinely has to come first.
Every activity must list ``aligned_objectives`` (existing ILO ids it practices, TLA = Teaching/
Learning Activity, drawn ONLY from YOUR ASSIGNED BLOCK's objectives) and
``prepares_for_assessment`` (existing assessment item ids it prepares learners for).
``materials_needed`` is free text, NOT an id — describe what content/resource would help, a
later step will source it. ``learner_cognitive_process`` must be one of: remember,
understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, create — and must be at or above the level of
every objective it aligns to (an Apply+ objective needs a hands-on activity: lab, exercise,
project, simulation — never only lecture/reading/video). ``prerequisite_activities`` may only
reference activity ids YOU produce in this same response — an activity in another block is not a
valid prerequisite here.
agentic.activities.persona: You are an expert learning-activity designer, responsible for how learners spend their time practising toward the objectives.
agentic.activities.task_block:
Design how learners spend their time: the instructional approach, and a grouping of the objectives into activity blocks. You write the APPROACH here; the activities themselves are written one block at a time, after this. The grouping is YOUR call and it decides how many Developer calls follow — group objectives a shared progression genuinely serves, and do not split for the sake of it.

The artifact you will submit must follow this EXACT schema:
{
  "instructional_strategies": {
    "model": "Gagné's 9 Events",
    "sequence": [
      {"event": "Gain attention", "activity": "<activity>", "duration": "<time>", "resources": ["<resource>"]},
      {"event": "Inform learners of objectives", "activity": "<activity>", "duration": "<time>", "resources": ["<resource>"]},
      {"event": "Stimulate recall of prior learning", "activity": "<activity>", "duration": "<time>", "resources": ["<resource>"]},
      {"event": "Present content", "activity": "<activity>", "duration": "<time>", "resources": ["<resource>"]},
      {"event": "Provide learning guidance", "activity": "<activity>", "duration": "<time>", "resources": ["<resource>"]},
      {"event": "Elicit performance", "activity": "<activity>", "duration": "<time>", "resources": ["<resource>"]},
      {"event": "Provide feedback", "activity": "<activity>", "duration": "<time>", "resources": ["<resource>"]},
      {"event": "Assess performance", "activity": "<activity>", "duration": "<time>", "resources": ["<resource>"]},
      {"event": "Enhance retention and transfer", "activity": "<activity>", "duration": "<time>", "resources": ["<resource>"]}
    ],
    "methods": ["<method1>", "<method2>", "<method3>"],
    "rationale": "<strategy selection rationale>"
  },
  "non_instructional_strategies": {
    "motivation_strategies": ["<motivation1>", "<motivation2>"],
    "self_directed_learning": ["<self1>", "<self2>"],
    "support_strategies": ["<support1>", "<support2>"]
  },
  "dev_plan": {
    "activity_blocks": [
      {"set_id": "BLOCK-01", "objectives": ["ILO-01", "ILO-02"],
       "block_theme": "<what ties these activities together, e.g. a shared progression>",
       "expected_activities": 3,
       "rationale": "<why these objectives belong in one block, or why one alone>"}
    ]
  }
}

Must include ALL 9 Gagné events. Every part of this plan must serve the learning objectives
given — do not introduce content unrelated to them.

Every activity must list ``aligned_objectives`` (existing ILO ids it practices, TLA = Teaching/

understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, create — and must be at or above the level of

project, simulation — never only lecture/reading/video). ``prerequisite_activities`` lists

agentic.analysis.persona: You are an expert instructional analyst performing the Analysis phase of ADDIE. You do not design the course — you establish what the design will have to answer to.
agentic.assessment.developer.assessment_:
Do NOT write an id for the artifacts you produce — ids are assigned when your set is
committed, so that two Developers working at the same time cannot name the same thing.
YOUR ASSIGNED SET below states how many items to write: cover every (objective, plan_category)
pair it lists with at least one item, and write no filler beyond the stated count. If the set spans
more than one objective, its items must share a common stem/scenario (the instrument the set
describes), but each individual item still carries a SINGLE ``aligned_objective`` — never a list.
required_cognitive_process must be one of:
remember, understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, create — and must be honestly achievable by the
item's format (a multiple_choice/true_false item cannot honestly claim apply-or-higher; use
short_answer or performance_task for that). Every Apply-or-higher objective must be measured by
a performance_task or short_answer item, never multiple_choice/true_false alone.
The question must make the learner PERFORM the required_cognitive_process on the subject matter
itself. Never write meta-questions that ask the learner to name, identify, or describe which
cognitive process, Bloom level, or objective is involved (e.g. "Which cognitive process is
required to ...?"), and never restate an objective's wording as the question -- ask for the
performance the objective describes.
A selectable-response item is not administrable without its response set: every multiple_choice
or matching item must carry ``options`` (the actual answer choices, plausible distractors
included) and ``correct_answer`` (the right option, verbatim); every true_false item must carry
``correct_answer``. short_answer and performance_task items take no options — their
scoring_criteria carry the judgment instead.
Give every item you write at least one entry in its own ``rubric`` list — the criterion goes
INSIDE the item, never in a separate list. ``description`` must be observable and scorable
(avoid vague words like "good"/"appropriate" without a rubric/score/percent/criteria anchor).
``evidence_type`` must be one of: true_false, matching, multiple_choice, quiz, short_answer,
performance_task — and must be achievable by that item's own ``type`` (do not require
performance_task evidence from a multiple_choice item).
agentic.assessment.persona: You are an expert assessment designer, responsible for how mastery of each learning objective will be evidenced and measured.
agentic.assessment.task_block:
Decide how you will know learners met each objective, and group the plan's coverage targets into instrument sets. You write the STRATEGY here; the items themselves are written one set at a time, after this. The grouping is YOUR call and it decides how many Developer calls follow — group work that one instrument genuinely covers together, and do not split for the sake of it.

The artifact you will submit must follow this EXACT schema:
{
  "assessment_plan": {
    "diagnostic": ["<diagnostic intent 1>", "<diagnostic intent 2>"],
    "formative": ["<formative intent 1>", "<formative intent 2>"],
    "summative": ["<summative intent 1>", "<summative intent 2>"],
    "lo_coverage_targets": {"ILO-01": ["diagnostic", "summative"], "ILO-02": ["formative", "summative"]},
    "expected_evidence": {"ILO-01": "<what evidence would demonstrate mastery of ILO-01>"},
    "formative_methods": ["<method1>", "<method2>", "<method3>"],
    "pilot_data_plan": {
      "collection_points": ["<when during the pilot run data is captured, e.g. 'after module 2'>"],
      "anticipated_difficulties": [
        {"area": "<the objective or content module learners are most likely to struggle with>",
         "rationale": "<why this is expected to be hard for THESE learners>",
         "detected_by": "<which formative method above would surface it>",
         "first_revision": "<the concrete first-round change to make if it does>"}
      ]
    }
  },
  "dev_plan": {
    "instrument_sets": [
      {"set_id": "SET-01", "objectives": ["ILO-01", "ILO-02"], "plan_categories": ["formative"],
       "expected_items": 2,
       "instrument_hint": "<what kind of instrument, e.g. one integrated case scenario>",
       "rationale": "<why these objectives/categories belong in one instrument, or why one alone>"}
    ]
  }
}

lo_coverage_targets and expected_evidence must have one entry per learning objective given.
formative_methods must each name an instrument and a cadence (e.g. "exit tickets after each
module"), consistent with the formative intent above.
pilot_data_plan.anticipated_difficulties must name at least two SPECIFIC areas, each anchored to
BOTH the content module or session where learners would struggle AND the objective id affected
(e.g. "Module 3 (interactive content design) — ILO-02", never "general comprehension"), each
with a rationale grounded in the learner profile and a first_revision that is concrete enough
to act on without further analysis.

Every (objective, plan_category) pair the assessment plan's lo_coverage_targets names needs at
least one item; the dev plan's expected_items says how many each instrument set writes, and
there is no filler beyond that. Do not aim for a round number of items -- a plan covering three
objectives in two categories needs six items, not ten. required_cognitive_process must be one of:
remember, understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, create — and must be honestly achievable by the
item's format (a multiple_choice/true_false item cannot honestly claim apply-or-higher; use
short_answer or performance_task for that). Every Apply-or-higher objective must be measured by
a performance_task or short_answer item, never multiple_choice/true_false alone.
The question must make the learner PERFORM the required_cognitive_process on the subject matter
itself. Never write meta-questions that ask the learner to name, identify, or describe which
cognitive process, Bloom level, or objective is involved (e.g. "Which cognitive process is
required to ...?"), and never restate an objective's wording as the question -- ask for the
performance the objective describes.
A selectable-response item is not administrable without its response set: every multiple_choice
or matching item must carry ``options`` (the actual answer choices, plausible distractors
included) and ``correct_answer`` (the right option, verbatim); every true_false item must carry
``correct_answer``. short_answer and performance_task items take no options — their
scoring_criteria carry the judgment instead.

agentic.content.developer.learner_materi:
Do NOT write an id for the artifacts you produce — ids are assigned when your set is
committed, so that two Developers working at the same time cannot name the same thing.
Produce materials ONLY for the ONE content module given — ``linked_module`` must be that
module's id on every material. YOUR ASSIGNED MODULE below states how many materials to write:
realize every media selection given for this module with at least one material, and write no
filler beyond the stated count. Each material's ``type`` must be the ``media_type`` of the
media selection it realizes — one of video, slides, simulation, document, audio — and its ``format`` a delivery format for
that type, respecting the constraints those media declared. Do not copy the type from the schema
example: it is a placeholder, and your module's own media list above is what decides.
``content`` must BE the learner-facing substance of the material, ready to hand to a learner —
the actual text, worked example, exercise instructions, or a scene-by-scene script for
video/slides — several sentences of scenario-specific detail, never a one-line description of
what the content would contain. Because you are developing one module at a time, give this
module's materials the full length and detail a learner would actually need.
agentic.content.persona: You are an expert content designer, responsible for the modules, media and materials the activities need.
agentic.content.task_block:
Decide how the content is organised and what form it takes: the modules and the media that realise them. The materials themselves are produced one module at a time, after this.

The artifact you will submit must follow this EXACT schema:
{
  "content_modules": [
    {"id": "MOD-01", "title": "<module title>", "description": "<what this module covers>", "supports_activities": ["TLA-01"], "covers_topics": ["TOP-01"], "expected_materials": 2}
  ],
  "media_selections": [
    {"id": "MED-01", "media_type": "video", "purpose": "<purpose>", "rationale": "<rationale>", "respects_constraints": ["CON-01"], "for_modules": ["MOD-01"]}
  ]
}

Every content module must set ``supports_activities`` to existing activity ids whose
``materials_needed`` hint it is addressing — do not invent a module nothing needs. Every module
should set ``covers_topics`` to existing topic ids. Every media selection should set
``respects_constraints`` to existing constraint ids it was chosen in light of (e.g. avoid
bandwidth-heavy video under a low-bandwidth constraint). media_type must be one of:
video, slides, simulation, document, audio. Every media selection should also set ``for_modules`` to
the content module id(s) it serves — a later step develops materials one module at a time and
needs to know which media belong to which module.

``expected_materials`` is how many learner materials that module actually needs — you are the only
step that knows whether a module is one handout or a broad topic needing several. At least one
per media selection the module receives, at most 6; a module that needs more than
that is really two modules.

Every material's ``linked_module`` must name an existing content module id it belongs to, and
its ``type`` must be the ``media_type`` of the media selection it realizes — one of
video, slides, simulation, document, audio — with ``format`` a delivery format for that type.
``content`` must BE the learner-facing substance of the material, ready to hand to a learner —
the actual text, worked example, exercise instructions, or a scene-by-scene script for
video/slides — several sentences of scenario-specific detail, never a one-line description of
what the content would contain.

    "support_procedures": ["<support1>", "<support2>"],
    "escalation_process": "<escalation process description>"
  }
}

Implementation requirements:
- instructor_orientation must be for instructors/operators, not learner learning objectives.
- system_check must include concrete learning platform, lab/resource access, login, network, data capture, accessibility, and fallback checks.
- prototype_execution must describe a realistic pilot, participant sample, execution records, issues, success criteria, and data collection.
- monitoring must include operational support, issue resolution, and real-time instructional adjustments.
- instructor_guide and operator_manual must reference the actual activities/materials given, not generic boilerplate.
- Every session guide must list the EXACT ids it delivers in ``activity_ids`` and hands out in
  ``material_ids`` (e.g. "TLA-01", "MAT-03"), as ids only, separate from the prose in
  ``activities``. Between them, the session guides should account for every activity and every
  material in the design — anything you leave out is something nobody scheduled.
- Write every session guide out in full (real objectives, what actually happens, real notes) and
  make operator_manual.system_setup concrete, stepwise setup instructions for THIS delivery
  environment (platform, accounts, tools, resources named in the scenario) that an operator
  could follow verbatim.

agentic.outcomes.persona: You are an expert instructional designer working on the Design phase of ADDIE, responsible for the course goal and learning objectives.
agentic.outcomes.task_block:
State what this course is for and what learners will be able to do, grounded in the analysis already in the design graph.

The artifact you will submit must follow this EXACT schema:
{
  "course_goal": {"statement": "<one overarching goal for the whole course/program>"},
  "learning_objectives": [
    {"id": "ILO-01", "level": "<bloom level>", "statement": "<objective>", "bloom_verb": "<verb>"},
    {"id": "ILO-02", "level": "<bloom level>", "statement": "<objective>", "bloom_verb": "<verb>"}
  ]
}

Each objective (ILO = Intended Learning Outcome) decomposes course_goal and is grounded in the
gaps/topics/learner profile given.

Return at least 1 objective; never an empty list. Beyond that YOU decide how many the scenario
needs. Derive that number from the analysis: every gap and topic identified must be addressed by
at least one objective, at a grain the stated duration, scope and learner profile can
realistically deliver. A short workshop and a semester-long course do not need the same number.
Do not pad to a round number, and do not merge unrelated gaps into one objective to hit a count.

Set each objective's ``level`` from the performance its gap actually demands, not from a
fixed progression. A gap about professional judgement yields an evaluate-level objective even if
no lower-level objective precedes it; a gap about terminology yields a remember-level one even if
it is the only such objective.

``level`` must be one of: remember, understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, create.
Use only these bloom_verb values: recall, explain, apply, analyze, evaluate, design.

checks.messages.bloom:
- LO 'ILO-02' has no bloom_verb — nothing states which cognitive level it targets, so no assessment item or activity can be checked against it.
  Fix: Set bloom_verb to the Bloom's verb the statement already performs (analyze, differentiate, examine, compare, contrast, organize), and set level to that verb's own Bloom level.
- LO 'ILO-03' uses bloom_verb 'grok', which is in none of Bloom's six levels, and its statement contains no taxonomy verb either — the objective's cognitive level cannot be read from either field.
  Fix: Replace bloom_verb with an evaluate-level verb (evaluate, judge, justify, assess, critique, argue) and restate the objective around it.
- LO 'ILO-04' declares level 'synthesis', which is not one of Bloom's six (remember, understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, create) — every Bloom cross-check reads this field and skips an objective it cannot place, so this objective is going unchecked.
  Fix: Set level to 'create', the level its own bloom_verb 'design' belongs to.
- LO 'ILO-05' declares level 'create' but its bloom_verb 'recall' is a remember-level verb — the two fields name different cognitive processes, and every downstream check reads level.
  Fix: Either set level to 'remember', or replace bloom_verb with a create-level verb (design, create, formulate, develop, compose, plan).
checks.messages.bloom_mismatch_activity:
- Objective 'ILO-01' targets apply, but of the 1 activity/activities practising it (TLA-0101), the highest learner_cognitive_process is understand — learners never rehearse at the level they are assessed on.
  Fix: Set learner_cognitive_process to 'apply' on at least one of TLA-0101 and make the activity actually require it (an apply-level task, not a walkthrough of one) — or add such an activity aligned to ILO-01.
checks.messages.bloom_mismatch_assessmen:
- Objective 'ILO-01' states an apply-level performance, but the best of the 1 item(s) measuring it (AT-0101) only reaches remember — an objective measured below its own level is not measured.
  Fix: On at least one of AT-0101, set required_cognitive_process to 'apply' AND give it a format that can carry it (short_answer or a performance task; matching, multiple_choice, quiz, true_false cap out below it) — or add a new apply-level item aligned to ILO-01.
checks.messages.evaluation_quality:
- Assessment plan declares formative intent but names no concrete data-collection method.
  Fix: List concrete formative methods (observation checklist, exit tickets, rubric checkpoints) under assessment_plan.formative_methods.
- Pilot data plan is missing or thin: it needs concrete collection points and at least two anticipated difficulties, each naming an area and a first revision.
  Fix: Fill assessment_plan.pilot_data_plan with collection_points and >=2 anticipated_difficulties ({area, rationale, detected_by, first_revision}), each naming a real objective or content module.
checks.messages.evidence_alignment:
- Rubric criterion 'RC-01' expects 'performance_task' evidence but 'AT-0101' can't produce it.
  Fix: Either loosen the criterion's evidence type or change the item's format.
checks.messages.item_completeness:
- Item 'AT-0101' is multiple_choice but has no options or correct_answer — it cannot be administered as written.
  Fix: Add the answer options (plausible distractors included) and the correct answer, or reformat the item as short_answer.
checks.messages.orphan_content:
- content:MOD-01 supports no Activity (orphan content module).
  Fix: Link this module to an existing Activity, or remove it.
- material:MAT-0101 has no source content module (orphan material).
  Fix: Set linked_module to an existing content module.
checks.messages.plan_coverage:
- The assessment plan promises a diagnostic item for ILO-01, but no assessment item realises that pair.
  Fix: Add a diagnostic assessment item aligned to ILO-01.
checks.messages.rubric_consistency:
- Rubric criterion 'RC-01' lacks an observable scoring description.
  Fix: Replace vague language with observable, scorable descriptors.
